## Overview

This model estimates a smooth association between phoneme blending and word reading. A Hilbert-space Gaussian process (HSGP) allows the slope to vary across the observed blending range. The exposure uses the bounded-score logit transform, and the declared sampling target is `target_accept=0.999`.

The specification uses a smaller HSGP basis and an `InverseGamma(8, 8)` lengthscale prior in response to earlier sampling problems. These choices do not show that the current fit converged or that the association changes slope. Nonlinear shape summaries require zero divergences and all other publication checks to pass.

## Adjustment set

Revised DAG (2026-07-10), derived by a backdoor d-separation search with the latent general ability ($GA$) held (the criterion that reproduces LRP56/58 and dose-077). In the DAG, phoneme blending ($PA$) has parents $\{A, GA, HS, IG, IS, TE, EV, SP, LS, RW\}$; the selected measured adjustment set is $\{A, HS, IG, IS, LS, TE, EV, SP, RW\}$, with $W_{\text{pre}}$ the autoregressive baseline.

**Adjustment for letter-sound knowledge.** The set includes **letter sounds** ($LS = L$): $LS \to PA$ and $LS \to WR$ make it a $PA \leftarrow LS \to WR$ confounder, so a blending -> reading association must be read **net of** letter-sound knowledge. Measure confounders $L$, $TE$, $E$ enter on their logit scale; the continuous confounders $HS$, $IS$ (`attend`), $SP$ and $RW$ enter as covariates; group $G\,(= IG)$ is the always-in precision term. The causal paths $PA \to WR$ and $PA \to NW \to WR$ are preserved ($NW$, $PS$ are descendants of $PA$ and are never adjusted).

_Adjusted association, not causal._ Residual confounding by latent general ability ($GA$) remains, so $f^B$ is an **adjusted association**, not a causal effect. The corresponding randomised-arm result is an available-case modified ITT estimate in the ITT suite.
